tagline: Up onto the tundra and over the Divide, summers only.
intro: From the Beaver Meadows entrance near Estes Park the road climbs onto Trail Ridge, a high, flat spur running east from the main range, and keeps to it all the way to Fall River Pass. The Arapaho called the old trail up here "Where the Children Walked". It was too steep to carry them.

The pavement tops out at 12,183 feet, higher than any other paved through-road in the country. Wildflowers cover the tundra in midsummer, and elk and bighorn sheep can usually be spotted crossing the meadows. Then the road crosses the Continental Divide at Milner Pass and goes down the Kawuneeche Valley beside the North Fork of the Colorado River to Grand Lake.

moments.title: Beaver Meadows Visitor Center
moments.text: Park headquarters since 1967, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright's firm after his death, with sandstone slabs set into its concrete and an old Snogo snow plow on display.

moments.title: Alpine Visitor Center
moments.text: At 11,796 feet on Fall River Pass it is the highest visitor center in the National Park System, and a quarter-mile round-trip trail from it goes by the name Huffer's Hill.

moments.title: Poudre Lake
moments.text: Just east of the Divide the Cache la Poudre River starts from a lake by the road. It freezes solid every winter, so no fish live in it.

practical: The high section of the road is closed from October to May and normally opens by Memorial Day weekend, weather permitting. The road status line is 970-586-1222.
